newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban says counter-attack repelled, jet downed.
newsitem.headline: Taleban says counter-attack repelled, jet downed.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic militia said it had pushed back a major opposition counter-offensive north of the capital Kabul on Wednesday and shot down an attacking jet fighter.
"We repulsed a heavy attack of the enemy which has been going on since early morning," a Taleban commander, Mullah Azizullah Agha, told Reuters in the town of Charikar.
He gave no casualty figures. Aid workers said they had taken at least five wounded Taleban fighters to Kabul.
Official Kabul radio said Taleban gunners shot down an "enemy" jet over frontlines north of Kabul. It gave no details.

The Taleban seized Charikar, about 50 km (30 miles) from Kabul, the nearby Soviet-built Bagram military airbase and much of Kapisa province last week from forces led by General Abdul Rashid Dostum and ousted government commander Ahmad Shah Masood.
Agha said the opposition assault, the first since the Taleban advance, had not changed the front lines.
It followed three opposition air raids on Kabul overnight and Wednesday morning, mainly targeting the airport.
Witnesses said at least three bombs fell on the airport, in a northeastern district of the Afghan capital, damaging the apron and the terminal building but leaving the runway intact.
Another bomb fell on waste ground inside the perimeter of the battered airport, used for military and civilian purposes.
"The runway is functioning and ready for flights," airport manager Mizbahullah Nuri told Reuters.
Opposition planes screamed over Kabul twice on Tuesday night and woke residents up again at 5.10 a.m. (0040 GMT). It was not immediately clear if bombs had hit other areas of the city.

Charikar is the provincial capital of Parwan province, long controlled by Masood and close to his Panjsher Valley stronghold to the northeast. It lies on the main road linking Kabul to the Salang Pass, the gateway to Dostum's northern heartland.
Taleban sources said Dostum's planes had bombed Charikar four times on Wednesday but there were no casualties.

Thousands of Charikar residents have been leaving the town in the past few days. More than 350 trucks, buses and other vehicles were seen carrying fleeing civilians towards Kabul during the 90-minute drive to Charikar on Wednesday.
Shops and the main hospital were shut in the wintry town, which appeared deserted apart from a few Taleban fighters and some trucks waiting to evacuate civilians to Kabul.

By noon the fighting had subsided, but the two sides were still trading artillery and mortar fire. Residents said three civilians had been wounded in the morning clashes, which took place within machinegun range of the town.
